title_plain: Rules of the Sea -- COLREGS and the Language a Regulation Uses

hero_line: The rules are short. What decides the question is who is reported to have said what.

reading_sub: A near miss in fog, and the three accounts that do not agree

paras: At 0240 a container ship and a fishing vessel passed within 0.2 of a nautical mile of each other inside a traffic separation scheme off a busy headland. Visibility at the time was reported as half a mile in fog. Neither vessel altered course until the final two minutes, neither made the sound signal that the rules require in those conditions, and no distress call was transmitted. There was no collision and no damage, which is the only reason the case was investigated rather than tried.

The regulation is not ambiguous. Rule 19 states that a vessel which detects the presence of another vessel by radar alone shall determine whether a close-quarters situation is developing and, if so, shall take avoiding action in ample time. The manual carried on the bridge reproduced the wording almost verbatim, and the master confirmed that he had read it during his last certificate renewal.

The officer of the watch on the container ship told investigators that he had seen the echo forty minutes before the encounter and that he had expected the other vessel to keep clear, because, in his words, she was the give-way vessel in a crossing situation. He was wrong twice. In restricted visibility the crossing rules do not apply and there is no stand-on vessel: both ships are required to act. He also stated that the lookout had been stood down at midnight, which the master denied.

The report concludes that a proper lookout was not maintained, that no sound signal was made at the prescribed intervals, and that the anchor watch schedule still in use on board had never been amended after the vessel entered restricted waters. It recommends that the operator review the way bridge manning is recorded, and observes that a rule read once every five years is not a rule that is known.

the reporting verb carries the writer's own position. Confirmed, stated, claimed, alleged and denied are not interchangeable: swap one for another and you change who the text believes. That swap is a whole question.
grammar_insight: In an investigation everything a person says arrives inside a reporting verb. The clause after that tells you WHAT was said; the verb before it tells you what the writer thinks of it. Read the verb first.

quickfire.situation: An option says: the master admitted that the lookout had been stood down. Is that what the text says?
tips: No. The officer stated it and the master DENIED it.
The reported clause is the same; the reporting verb is the opposite.

quickfire.situation: Rule 19 says a vessel shall take avoiding action. Is shall the future here?
tips: No. In a regulation shall is an obligation: read it as must.
The rules never say must, and the paper counts on that.

quickfire.situation: Say, in exam register, that nobody was properly watching.
tips: The requirement to keep a lookout was not discharged.
A proper lookout was not maintained.

quickfire.situation: The officer thought the other ship was the give-way vessel. Give both reasons why he was wrong.
tips: In restricted visibility the crossing rules do not apply.
There is no stand-on vessel: both ships are required to act.

quickfire.situation: Turn this into reported speech: I saw the echo forty minutes ago.
tips: He said that he had seen the echo forty minutes earlier.
Ago becomes earlier, and the past becomes the past perfect.

quickfire.situation: Which of these tells you the writer does NOT accept the statement: confirmed, stated, alleged?
tips: Alleged. It marks the claim as unproven.
Confirmed accepts it; stated is neutral.

listenings.sub: The man who saw the echo, in his own words. Sound first -- no text.
listenings.text: I had the echo at two o'clock, maybe a little after. It was steady, fine on the starboard bow, and I plotted it twice. I judged that she was crossing and that under the rules she was the one who had to keep out of my way, so I held my course. I know now that that was wrong, and I have said so. In fog the crossing rules do not apply at all. Both of us should have slowed down and both of us should have been sounding. What I will not accept is the suggestion that there was nobody on lookout. I have told the investigators the same thing four times: the lookout was stood down at midnight because the master told me to send him to the forward store, and if that is denied, then one of us is not remembering the night the way it happened.
questions: What did he see, when, and what did he do about it?
He had a steady radar echo at about two o'clock, fine on the starboard bow. He plotted it twice, judged that the other vessel had to keep out of his way, and held his course.
What does he now accept was wrong?
That in fog the crossing rules do not apply at all. Both vessels should have slowed down and both should have been sounding.
What is the one point he refuses to accept?
The suggestion that there was nobody on lookout. He says the lookout was stood down at midnight because the master told him to send the man to the forward store.

listenings.sub: An examiner reads Rule 19 the way it has to be read. Sound first -- no text.
listenings.text: Candidates lose marks on Rule 19 for one reason: they read it as if it were the crossing rule with fog added. It is not. Rule 19 applies when vessels are not in sight of one another in or near an area of restricted visibility, and it replaces the steering rules entirely. There is no give-way vessel and there is no stand-on vessel. Every vessel shall proceed at a safe speed adapted to the prevailing circumstances. Every vessel which detects another by radar alone shall determine whether a close-quarters situation is developing, and if so shall take avoiding action in ample time. And note the word shall. In this document shall is not the future. It is an obligation, and there is no version of the rule in which it is optional. If you can say those three things, you can answer any question they set on Rule 19.
questions: What is the mistake candidates make with Rule 19?
They read it as if it were the crossing rule with fog added. It is not: Rule 19 replaces the steering rules entirely, and there is no give-way vessel and no stand-on vessel.
What are the two duties she names for every vessel?

Every vessel shall proceed at a safe speed adapted to the circumstances, and every vessel that detects another by radar alone shall determine whether a close-quarters situation is developing and take avoiding action in ample time.
What does she say about the word shall?
In this document shall is not the future. It is an obligation, and there is no version of the rule in which it is optional.

roleplays.label: Guided
roleplays.scenario: Report the case in five sentences, in this order: what happened and where, what the regulation requires, what the officer told the investigators, what the master denied, and what the report concluded. Use a different reporting verb in each of the last three.

roleplays.label: Semi-free
roleplays.h: Whose Word Does the Text Take?
roleplays.scenario: The text reports three people. Say, for each one, what was reported and whether the writer accepts it, rejects it or stays neutral -- and name the verb that proves your answer. You may not use the word said.

roleplays.label: Free
roleplays.scenario: Close the text. Explain out loud what Rule 19 requires and why the officer's reasoning failed, as if you were telling a candidate who is sitting the same paper next month. Then say what the report would have looked like if there had been a collision.
roleplays.note: No support. Target: the three duties of Rule 19, plus the two reasons the crossing rules did not apply.

wrap_head: You Read Who Said It, and Who Is Believed
survival: Neither vessel altered course, and no sound signal was made at the prescribed intervals.
Rule 19 states that a vessel shall take avoiding action in ample time.
The officer told investigators that he had seen the echo forty minutes before the encounter.
In restricted visibility there is no stand-on vessel, and both ships are required to act.
The report concludes that a proper lookout was not maintained.
checklist: I know what a give-way vessel and a stand-on vessel are, and when neither exists.
I read shall in a regulation as an obligation, not as the future.
I can turn direct speech into reported speech with the right backshift.
I can tell confirmed from stated from denied, and say what each one does to the claim.
I can report a set of conflicting accounts in my own words.
badge_line: The regulation was never the hard part. Who is reported to have said what -- that is the question.

pc_desc: The words a collision regulation is written in and the reported speech an investigation uses. Key words: collision, visibility, give-way vessel, stand-on vessel, restricted waters, lookout, sound signal, distress, anchor watch, traffic separation scheme. Structure: reported speech in technical documentation.

paras: The officer of the watch told investigators that he had seen the echo forty minutes before the encounter and that he had expected the other vessel to keep clear. The master confirmed that he had read the manual during his last certificate renewal.

The officer also stated that the lookout had been stood down at midnight, which the master denied. Rule 19 states that a vessel which detects another by radar alone shall determine whether a close-quarters situation is developing. The report observes that a rule read once every five years is not a rule that is known.

quiz.q: Why is it he had seen the echo and not he saw the echo?
opts: Because the reporting verb is in the past, so the verb inside moves one step back.
Because seeing an echo is a permanent state.
Because the past perfect is more polite in a report.

quiz.q: Why does Rule 19 states that a vessel shall determine keep its verb in the present?
opts: Because the writer forgot to backshift it.
Because a regulation is true now, not only at the moment it was quoted.
Because shall cannot be put in the past in English.

quiz.q: He stated that the lookout had been stood down, which the master denied. What does the text tell you?
opts: That the lookout was certainly stood down.
That the lookout was certainly not stood down.
That the two accounts conflict, and the text does not settle it.

teacher.s1: Abertura (2 min): DECISAO DE DESENHO, valida para o programa inteiro: toda aula e reading-driven, sem alternar com aula de fala (a REGRA 29.2 nao se aplica aqui), porque a prova e 100% leitura. Entre direto, sem cumprimento scriptado (REGRA 27A).
teacher.s2: Homework check + warm-up (5 min): Ela leu as Regras 13, 14 e 15 e escreveu tres frases. Peca que leia as tres. O que voce esta medindo: ela PARAFRASEOU ou copiou? Se copiou, e o diagnostico mais importante da aula -- e exatamente o que a prova nao aceita. Nao corrija; anote.
teacher.s3: Provocacao (5 min): As tres frases so diferem no verbo. Espere ela nomear a mudanca sozinha. Se travar, pergunte: after which of the three do you believe the master? Este slide e a aula inteira em miniatura.
teacher.s4: Objetivo (2 min): Diga: the words of the rule, the verb that reports it, and why a regulation never says must.
teacher.s5: Transicao vocab (1 min): Diga: Ten words, and four of them only exist inside the rules. Passe ao proximo.
teacher.s6: Vocab reveal 1-4 (5 min): collision, visibility, give-way vessel, stand-on vessel. NAO traduza (REGRA 13). CCQ decisivo: If I am the stand-on vessel, do I change course? (No -- you hold course and speed, and THAT is the duty.) E o contraintuitivo que derruba candidato.
teacher.s7: Vocab reveal 5-7 (5 min): restricted waters, lookout, sound signal. CCQ para lookout: Is a lookout only about seeing? (No -- by sight AND by hearing, e o texto da Regra 5 diz isso.) CCQ para sound signal: Is it a warning or a message? (A message: it says what you are doing.)
teacher.s8: Vocab reveal 8-10 (5 min): distress, anchor watch, traffic separation scheme. CCQ para distress: Is a ship without fuel in distress? (Only if there is grave and imminent danger -- a palavra e tecnica e o edital cobra o sentido tecnico.) Explique a TSS com a mao: duas faixas de sentido unico separadas por uma zona.
teacher.s9: Consolidate (4 min): Ela toca a palavra e le a definicao em voz alta antes de fechar o par. Se errar, reformule a definicao em vez de dar a resposta.
teacher.s10: Transicao leitura (1 min): Diga: Three people tell this story and they do not agree. O proximo slide e o de TAREFA: a pergunta ANTES do texto.
teacher.s11: Leitura (7 min): Tres minutos em silencio, sem dicionario. NAO traduza. Depois peca UMA frase de resumo. O detalhe fica para o true/false.
teacher.s12: Gist (3 min): Ela escolhe e JUSTIFICA. A opcao (c) e a armadilha: e a conclusao que o proprio oficial tirou, e o texto diz que ele estava errado.
teacher.s13: True or False (7 min): REGRA DA CASA: TRUE ou FALSE e DEPOIS a linha do texto que prova, em voz alta. A afirmacao 1 e conversao de unidade (0.2 milha = 2 cabos) e a 4 e troca de verbo de reporte (denied vs corroborated) -- as duas caem em prova.
teacher.s14: Transicao gramatica (1 min): Diga: Now the verb that decides everything. Passe ao proximo.
teacher.s15: Grammar discovery (7 min): Nao de a regra. Pergunte quais dos quatro reportam uma PESSOA e qual reporta um DOCUMENTO, e por que so um mantem o presente. So entao clique Reveal the Rule. CCQ: If an option says 'the master admitted that the lookout had been stood down', is that in the text? (No -- ele NEGOU.) Ela estuda gramatica sozinha: aqui e ferramenta de leitura, nao producao.
teacher.s16: Practice (4 min): Ela diz a forma ORALMENTE antes de clicar. Se travar, pergunte: person or document?
teacher.s17: Spot the error (4 min): Os quatro classicos: told TO, said ME, shall TO, e falta de backshift (has seen por had seen).
teacher.s18: Transicao equivalencia (1 min): Diga: Same night, other words. Passe ao proximo.
teacher.s19: Como a prova esconde (4 min): Os quatro pares saiam do texto. Pergunte, para cada um: which of the two is on the page?
teacher.s20: Equivalencia (5 min): Depois de fechar os pares, cubra a coluna da direita e faca a direcao dificil: dada a frase simples, como a prova escreveria?
teacher.s21: Complete (5 min): Teacher-led. Leia em voz alta e pare em cada lacuna. As oito respostas sao oito das dez palavras da aula.
teacher.s22: Quick fire (6 min): Uma por vez, em voz alta, antes das dicas. A ultima (confirmed / stated / alleged) e a mais valiosa do programa inteiro.
teacher.s23: Transicao (1 min): Diga: The officer, and then the rule itself. Passe ao proximo.
teacher.s24: Listening 1 (5 min): LEIA AS 3 PERGUNTAS EM VOZ ALTA COM ELA ANTES de tocar (REGRA 2.1). Escuta medida em 0%: comece em 0.75x. Toque duas vezes, sem texto. Depois pergunte: he says the master told him to send the lookout away. Does the written report say that? (Nao -- o relatorio so diz que o comandante NEGOU. E a mesma divergencia, do outro lado.)
teacher.s25: Listening 2 (5 min): LEIA AS 3 PERGUNTAS EM VOZ ALTA COM ELA ANTES de tocar (REGRA 2.1). Este audio e deliberadamente um examinador: e o resumo que ela precisa decorar da Regra 19. Peca que repita as tres coisas no fim, sem olhar.
teacher.s26: Role-play guiado (4 min): Cinco frases, cada uma com um verbo de reporte diferente. NAO corrija durante. Conte quantos verbos DIFERENTES ela usou e diga o numero.
teacher.s27: Role-play semi-livre (5 min): Proibir 'said' e o exercicio: sem ele ela tem de escolher entre told, confirmed, stated e denied -- e escolher e ler.
teacher.s28: Producao livre (6 min): Nao interrompa. O que voce mede: ela nomeia as tres obrigacoes da Regra 19 e os DOIS motivos pelos quais as regras de cruzamento nao valiam.
teacher.s29: Transicao wrap-up (1 min): Diga: Let us see what you can do now.
teacher.s30: Survival card (3 min): Cinco frases do proprio texto. Toque e peca repeticao. Insista em 'avoiding action' e 'prescribed intervals' -- sao colocacoes, nao palavras soltas.
teacher.s31: Checklist (2 min): Leia cada item em voz alta. Os 5 checks fecham a aula e acendem o stamp.
teacher.s32: Encerramento (2 min): Diga: Lesson 3 complete, Helena. HOMEWORK ORALMENTE, nunca escrito na tela: (1) ler as Regras 5, 6 e 19 do COLREGS em ingles e escrever tres frases de resumo com as PROPRIAS palavras, sem copiar; (2) pegar cinco frases do audio do oficial e reescreve-las como o relatorio escreveria, com verbo de reporte diferente em cada uma. Proxima aula: Cargo, Ports and Ship Operations.
